_note: Curated, citation-bearing content. Extracted measures live in .staging (produced by scripts/etl_analytics.py); this file is the editorial layer: what each dataset is, what controls must hold, and the audit facts that come from documents rather than from parquet. Every audit_posture row names its citation and whether it is a primary or secondary read.

datasets.label: Statement of Budgetary Resources (File A)
datasets.grain: Treasury Account Symbol x fiscal year
datasets.description: Budgetary resources, obligations incurred, unobligated balance and gross outlays at TAS grain, as submitted by reporting agencies. The backbone of the execution chain.
datasets.limitations: Carries five agency identifier codes; 011 (Executive Office of the President) is not the Department and is excluded from every DOW scope. The current fiscal year is a period-to-date submission, not a closed year.

datasets.label: Object Class and Program Activity (File B)
datasets.source_system: USASpending Account Breakdown by Program Activity and Object Class
datasets.grain: TAS x program activity x object class x fiscal year
datasets.description: Obligations decomposed into USSGL undelivered orders (480100 series) and delivered orders (490100 series), plus OMB object class. Shows what stage each obligated dollar has reached.
datasets.limitations: Object class is reported by the component; unreported and mixed classes appear as their own buckets rather than being redistributed.

datasets.label: President's Budget -1 exhibits (P-1, P-1R, R-1)
datasets.source_system: DoD Comptroller President's Budget justification books, PB2020-PB2027
datasets.grain: Budget line item x President's Budget year x fiscal year
datasets.description: Every procurement (P-1), reserve-equipment (P-1R) and RDT&E (R-1) budget line in the eight President's Budget books held here, at the grain the exhibits themselves publish: a book year and a fiscal year. Because each book restates three fiscal years -- prior-year actuals, current-year enacted, budget-year request -- a single fiscal year appears in three successive books with three different numbers, and all three are kept. The exhibit account symbol is resolved to a Treasury account so a budget line can be carried into the execution files, and the Department's own Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System book is carried alongside as its answer to which of these lines is a major program.
datasets.refresh_cadence: annual, on publication of each President's Budget
datasets.limitations: The P-1R exhibit is National Guard and Reserve equipment already counted inside the P-1 lines, and R-1 rows marked Include-in-TOA = N sit outside total obligation authority; both are kept, flagged is_memo, and excluded from every total. Amounts are in thousands of dollars as published, are total obligation authority rather than outlays, and are not comparable to the execution files without ageing prior-year balances. The link from a weapons-book system to a budget line is derived from shared type designators or shared significant words -- neither source carries the other's key -- and every link records the evidence it rests on.

datasets.label: Contract award transactions (FPDS)
datasets.grain: Contract action (transaction) x fiscal year x vintage
datasets.description: Federal action obligations for DoW contract actions. Two vintages are retained so that movement in closed fiscal years is measurable rather than assumed.
datasets.limitations: Federal action obligation is an FPDS reporting concept and is not the same measure as an account-linked obligation; see the reconciliation. The most recent fiscal year is incomplete.

datasets.label: Financial assistance transactions (cooperative agreements, grants, direct payments)
datasets.source_system: USASpending financial assistance archive, Department of War / Department of Defense awarding agency
datasets.grain: Assistance transaction x fiscal year x vintage
datasets.description: Federal action obligations for DoW financial-assistance awards — cooperative agreements, project and formula grants, and direct payments. A separate warehouse tree and reporting chain from contracts and File C; not account-linked and not reconciled against anything.
datasets.limitations: Rows are filtered to awarding-agency name ‘Department of Defense’ or ‘Department of War’ rather than an agency-identifier code, because this warehouse cut carries no code column. The assistance-type codes present are cooperative agreements, grants and direct payments — no loan or loan-guarantee type codes appear in this cut, so it is not a credit-programs picture and must not be described as one. Only two vintages are retained so far; vintage drift is measurable but thin.

datasets.label: Award-to-account linkage (File C)
datasets.grain: Award x TAS x fiscal year
datasets.description: Contract obligations that components have linked to a Treasury account. Compared against the award files to measure linkage completeness.
datasets.limitations: A low linkage percentage measures reporting completeness between two chains. It is not an estimate of unsupported or missing obligations, and must never be presented as one.

datasets.label: Program execution and account traceability
datasets.source_system: USASpending contract award archive; USASpending File C
datasets.grain: Acquisition program code x fiscal year
datasets.description: Contract obligations cut by FPDS dod_acquisition_program_code -- the only field in this warehouse keyed to a budget line rather than to an account -- with the share of each total whose funding Treasury account is actually named, the accounts named on those actions, contract-level concentration, and the File C tie-out for the same contracts.
datasets.limitations: FPDS records 'no acquisition program' as code 000 / description NONE, and roughly three quarters of DoD contract dollars carry that code, so this covers only the program-attributable quarter of the file -- dm_program_coverage states how much per year. federal_accounts_funding_this_award lists every account funding an award without apportioning the obligation across them, so no figure here is split by account. A program obligation total is not comparable to that program's appropriation: it draws on prior-year balances this cut cannot age, and Foreign Military Sales trust dollars (011-8242) sit on the same contract actions as Department appropriations.

datasets.label: DoD-FM knowledge bank and curated wiki
datasets.source_system: Local knowledge bank; curated DoD-FM wiki pages
datasets.description: Definitions with authorities, document inventory by collection, FY2027 justification exhibits, and the congressional hearing record.
datasets.limitations: Hearing dates are the acquisition date embedded in the GPO filename, not the date the hearing was held; they are labelled as ingest dates and never as hearing dates.

datasets.label: Budget line to acquisition program crosswalk
datasets.source_system: Derived from the President's Budget -1 exhibits and the FPDS contract archive
datasets.grain: Budget line item x FPDS acquisition program code
datasets.description: The join that lets a President's Budget line be followed into the contract file. The -1 exhibits name budget lines; FPDS names acquisition program codes; neither carries the other's key, so each row here records the evidence the link rests on -- a shared type designator, or identical names.
datasets.refresh_cadence: with each exhibit or contract refresh
datasets.limitations: Derived, not published by the Department. Only a shared type designator or an identical name is accepted, and a designator naming more than one program code produces no row rather than a guess -- so this covers the lines whose identity is unambiguous in both vocabularies and no others. A link means the two names refer to the same system, not that the budget line's appropriation funded the contracts under that code.

datasets.label: Audit posture (documentary)
datasets.source_system: DoD FY2025 Agency Financial Report; DoD OIG
datasets.description: Audit opinion, material weakness counts and scope limitations, read from the Agency Financial Report rather than inferred from file counts.
datasets.limitations: Read via the curated wiki summary of the AFR, which is a secondary read of a primary document. Each row records which it is.

controls.name: Status of budgetary resources foots
controls.assertion: Obligations incurred plus unobligated balance equals total budgetary resources, within 0.1%.
controls.rationale: The status section of the SBR must equal the resources section. A break means the extract has dropped or double-counted a TAS.
controls.authority: OMB Circular A-136; DoD FMR Vol 6A

controls.name: Budgetary resources components foot
controls.assertion: Appropriated authority, unobligated balance brought forward, adjustments, and other budgetary resources sum to total budgetary resources, within 0.5%.
controls.rationale: Proves the resources waterfall shown on the execution page is complete. Note that the source's other-budgetary-resources column already rolls up borrowing authority, contract authority and spending authority from offsetting collections; adding those separately double-counts them.

controls.name: Outlays do not exceed resources
controls.assertion: Gross outlays are less than or equal to total budgetary resources.
controls.rationale: An outlay above available resources indicates a scope or sign error, not an Antideficiency event in this dataset.

controls.name: File A and File B obligations agree
controls.assertion: Obligations incurred per File B are within 0.5% of File A for the same scope, fiscal year and submission period.
controls.rationale: File A and File B are separate submissions of the same execution at different grain. A variance is a cross-system reconciliation finding to be published and explained, not a reason to withhold the data - so this control reports rather than blocks.

controls.name: Department scope excludes non-Department agencies
controls.assertion: No DOW-scope figure includes agency identifier code 011.
controls.rationale: File A carries five agency codes. Including the Executive Office of the President in a Department total overstates it materially.
controls.authority: Treasury Account Symbol structure; OMB agency codes

controls.name: Linkage cannot exceed the population
controls.assertion: File C account-linked contract obligations do not exceed award-file obligations for the same fiscal year.
controls.rationale: Linkage above 100% would mean the subset is larger than the set, indicating a scope mismatch between the two chains.

controls.name: Every load carries a vintage
controls.assertion: Every current dm_load row has a non-null vintage and extraction timestamp.
controls.rationale: A figure without a vintage cannot be defended, reproduced, or compared against a later extract.

controls.name: Incomplete fiscal years are flagged
controls.assertion: Any fiscal year whose submission period is not P12 is marked as partial.
controls.rationale: An in-progress year shown beside closed years reads as collapsed execution unless it is labelled.

controls.name: Every definition carries an authority
controls.assertion: Every published definition names at least one authoritative source.
controls.rationale: A definitions registry without citations is an opinion, not a standard.

controls.name: Dimensional cuts do not exceed the fiscal-year total
controls.assertion: For each dimension, the sum of the retained top-N buckets does not exceed that fiscal year's award total.
controls.rationale: Guards the double-counting failure mode where a record increments more than one bucket.

controls.name: Assistance dimensional cuts do not exceed the fiscal-year total
controls.assertion: For each dimension, the sum of the retained top-N buckets does not exceed that fiscal year's assistance total.
controls.rationale: Same double-counting guard as AWD-01 (contract awards), applied to the assistance dimension cuts.

controls.name: Every program measure names a program and a vintage
controls.assertion: Every row in dm_program_fy carries a non-empty program_code that exists in dm_program_dim, and hangs off a dm_load row with a vintage.
controls.rationale: A program-level figure with no program identity or no vintage cannot be cited, corrected, or reproduced. This is the same provenance rule the rest of the site enforces by shape, asserted here because the program tables are the first cut keyed to a budget line rather than an account.

controls.name: No program obligation is apportioned across the accounts named on it
controls.assertion: For every fiscal year, the sum of dm_program_account.obligation for a program does not exceed that program's fiscal-year obligation.
controls.rationale: federal_accounts_funding_this_award lists every account funding an award and states no split. Summing a program's obligations by account would fabricate an apportionment the source does not contain -- the specific error this table exists to make impossible.

controls.name: Account-traceable share travels with every program obligation total
controls.assertion: Every dm_program_fy row carries traceable_obligation and untraceable_obligation summing to its obligation, with traceable_pct consistent with them.
controls.rationale: A program obligation published without the share of it that names a funding account reads as reconciled when it is not. In FY2025 only 7.6% of F-35 obligations name an account, so the total alone is the misleading figure and the pair is the honest one.

controls.name: Accounts outside Department scope are disclosed, not dropped
controls.assertion: Where an account outside agency codes 097/021/017/057 is named on a program's obligations, dm_program_account records it in out_of_scope_accounts rather than omitting the row.
controls.rationale: SCOPE-01 keeps agency 011 out of Department budgetary totals, and that is right for budget. On the execution side, Foreign Military Sales trust dollars (011-8242) sit on the same F-35 contract actions as Department appropriations. Dropping those rows would hide why a program's obligations are not comparable to its appropriation.

controls.name: In-progress program years are flagged period-to-date
controls.assertion: A program fiscal year is flagged partial exactly when it is the newest fiscal year in the current contract vintage.
controls.rationale: The newest year in the warehouse is always period-to-date. An unflagged partial year reads as a collapse in program spending rather than a year still being reported.

controls.name: Program-dimension coverage of the contract file is published
controls.assertion: dm_program_coverage carries one row per fiscal year in which attributed and unattributed obligations sum to the fiscal-year total, and attributed_pct is consistent with them.
controls.rationale: FPDS records 'no acquisition program' as the explicit code 000 with description NONE rather than as a null, so a null test finds almost nothing and makes program tagging look complete. It is not: roughly three quarters of DoD contract dollars carry no program at all. Publishing the coverage denominator stops the program pages from implying they cover the file.

controls.name: The three-year restatement structure survives the load
controls.assertion: For every fiscal year in dm_exhibit_program_fy, the number of distinct fy_role values equals the number of President's Budget books held that cover that year (a year is covered by the books for pb = fy, fy+1 and fy+2).
controls.rationale: Each -1 book restates three fiscal years in three roles: prior-year actuals, current-year enacted, budget-year request. A fiscal year therefore appears in three successive books with three different numbers, and the difference between them is the restatement history -- the one thing these exhibits carry that exists in no other source here. Any de-duplication that leaves a year with fewer roles than the books we hold would silently destroy it, so the load is blocked rather than published.
controls.authority: DoD Financial Management Regulation Volume 2A/2B, exhibit formats

controls.name: Every fiscal-year role is derived from the book it was read from
controls.assertion: For every row in dm_exhibit_line and dm_exhibit_program_fy, fy_role equals prior_actual when fiscal_year = pb_year - 2, enacted when fiscal_year = pb_year - 1, request when fiscal_year = pb_year, and other otherwise.
controls.rationale: The role is what turns a number into a claim: the same $6.9 billion is a request in one book, an enactment in the next and an actual in the third. If the role were inferred from a column heading it would drift with the heading, so it is derived arithmetically from the book year and this control asserts nothing overrode it.

controls.name: Memo-only lines are flagged and never enter a total
controls.assertion: No row of dm_exhibit_line with is_memo = false belongs to the P-1R exhibit or carries a cost type naming a memo non-add.
controls.rationale: The P-1R exhibit is National Guard and Reserve equipment already counted inside the P-1 lines, and R-1 rows outside total obligation authority are the same kind of restatement. Both are kept rather than dropped, because a total that silently omits an exhibit cannot be explained on the page; that only works if the flag is right, which is what this asserts.
controls.authority: DoD Financial Management Regulation Volume 2A, P-1R exhibit

controls.name: The per-line rollup foots to the exhibit rows it came from
controls.assertion: For every budget line, book year and fiscal year, dm_exhibit_program_fy.amount_k equals the sum of dm_exhibit_line.amount_k for the same key, within a thousandth of a percent.
controls.rationale: The rollup is what the page reads; the line rows are what the exhibit published. A rollup that does not foot to its own detail is a fabricated figure with a citation attached, which is worse than no figure, so the load is blocked.

controls.name: Every fiscal-year figure names the exhibit column it came from
controls.assertion: Every row of dm_exhibit_line carries a total_basis of total_column, sole_column or sum_of_components and a non-empty total_column label.
controls.rationale: The exhibits change shape between eras -- Base and OCO, Less Supplementals, Discretionary and Reconciliation -- and the broadest figure for a year is not always in the same place. Two rules pick it, and which one fired changes what the number means, so the basis is recorded per row and asserted here rather than assumed.

controls.name: The Treasury-account crosswalk is shaped and its coverage stated
controls.assertion: Every non-null treasury_account in dm_exhibit_program is three digits, a hyphen and four digits, and the share of budget lines that resolved to one is reported.
controls.rationale: The exhibit account symbol (1506N) and the Treasury account symbol (017-1506) differ only by the organisation letter, and that crosswalk is the whole bridge from a budget line to the execution files. A malformed symbol would join to nothing and read as an execution gap rather than as a parsing failure, so the shape is asserted and the coverage published beside it.
controls.authority: Treasury Financial Manual, agency and account symbols

controls.name: Weapons-book linkage is disclosed, not implied
controls.assertion: Every row of dm_exhibit_weapon_link names a match_method and the evidence it rests on, and the share of the newest book's weapon systems that reached a budget line is reported.
controls.rationale: Neither the weapons book nor the -1 exhibits carry the other's key, so every link here is derived. Publishing derived links without the evidence would let a reader mistake a name-similarity match for a Department-published mapping. Systems that reached no budget line are counted rather than hidden, because that count is the honest measure of how far this crosswalk goes.
controls.authority: Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System, DoD Comptroller

controls.name: The exhibit request totals tie to the Department's own weapons book
controls.assertion: For every President's Budget year whose Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System book states an investment breakdown, the non-memo P-1 request lines total the procurement figure it publishes and the non-memo R-1 request lines total the RDT&E figure, each within half of the last printed digit.
controls.rationale: Every other control here asks whether the extract is consistent with itself. This one asks whether it is right: the weapons book totals the same request from the same submission, so a disagreement means the extract has gained or lost money, not that the sources differ. It is what caught the P-1 advance-procurement subtotal being counted alongside the by-year detail it summarises -- a $14.4 billion double count in PB2026 alone that no internal check could have seen.
controls.authority: Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System, DoD Comptroller, Introduction

controls.name: Every budget-line to program-code link names its evidence
controls.assertion: Every row of dm_exhibit_program_link carries a match_method of designator or exact_name, non-empty evidence, and a budget line that exists in dm_exhibit_program.
controls.rationale: This crosswalk is the step that lets an appropriation be followed into a contract, which makes a wrong link worse than no link: it would put one program's contracts under another program's budget line. Nothing weaker than a shared type designator is accepted, an ambiguous designator produces no row, and every accepted row states what it rests on so a reader can reject one without distrusting the rest.

controls.name: Each weapon system's cost table foots to its own printed total
controls.assertion: For every weapon system and fiscal year, the appropriation blocks extracted from the page sum to the total the page prints, within the greater of $0.6M and 0.2%. At least 97% of system-years must foot.
controls.rationale: The Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System book prints a total beneath the appropriation blocks it is made of, so a page that does not foot has been read wrongly. The book changes shape between eras -- Base/OCO in PB2020-21, Discretionary/Mandatory in PB2026 -- and a column assigned to the wrong year publishes an OCO or reconciliation add as a whole year. A small number of pages are typeset so tightly that a figure cannot be assigned to a column at all; those are named rather than absorbed, which is why this is a threshold rather than an absolute.
controls.authority: Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System, FY2020-FY2026 President's Budget

controls.name: A weapon system's budget lines never exceed its published cost
controls.assertion: For each weapon system and book year, the non-memo request on every budget line tied to that system is compared with the system total the weapons book publishes. Neither direction is repaired; both are published on the system.
controls.rationale: This is the per-system form of EXH-08 and the only check on the weapon crosswalk that reaches outside the extract. A shortfall means the crosswalk has not found some of the system's spares, modification or support lines -- their titles carry no designator to tie back -- which is why no programme total on this site is presented as complete. An excess means a budget line is broader than the programme: the Next Generation Squad Weapon ammunition line funds ammunition the weapons-book page excludes, and one R-1 program element can fund several systems. The exhibits publish no split inside a line, so nothing here apportions one. The control exists to state the gap on the page beside the figures; it must never be satisfied by dropping links until the two numbers agree, which would be fitting the crosswalk to the answer.
controls.authority: Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System; P-1 and R-1 exhibits, FY2020-FY2027

controls.name: Every search abbreviation is one the weapons book itself expands
controls.assertion: Every row in the alias table names a system that exists in the weapons book, quotes the phrase the expansion was read from, and was made by one of the two recorded methods.
controls.rationale: The alias table is what lets a search for 'JSF' find the F-35. Its risk is not arithmetic -- no figure is ever aggregated through it -- but that an abbreviation quietly starts meaning something the Department never wrote. So an alias exists only where the book expands it into the system's own name, sharing two or more significant words with it, and the sentence is carried on the row so a reader can reject one alias without distrusting the rest. The same evidence test the weapon crosswalk uses.
controls.authority: Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System, FY2020-FY2026

controls.name: The File C figure is never published without the snapshots it was chosen over
controls.assertion: Every fiscal year with a published File C linkage figure carries its full submission-period series, and the published period appears in that series flagged as chosen.
controls.rationale: The published linkage figure is the product of a choice: the warehouse holds four File C snapshots per fiscal year and the extract publishes the one with the most rows, on the reasoning that it is the most complete copy held. That is a defensible rule and it is still a rule. This control is a shape rather than a check, in the sense PROG-03 is: it makes it structurally impossible for a page to render the headline without the rejected alternatives beside it, because a reader who cannot see the alternatives cannot know the headline was chosen.
controls.authority: DATA Act File C (award financial), USASpending account-level submissions

controls.name: How far the linkage figure moves between snapshots of the same year
controls.assertion: For each fiscal year, the linkage percentage is computed from every substantive File C snapshot held and the spread between the highest and lowest is published. A spread wider than a factor of two is reported as a finding.
controls.rationale: This control measures the size of the choice FILEC-01 exposes. Reading FY2022 at period 3 gives 1.4% linkage and at period 12 gives 11.6% — the same warehouse, the same year, an eight-fold difference. Where the spread is that wide, comparing one year's figure with another's is comparing two arbitrary picks, and a falling or rising line drawn through them measures the picks rather than the Department. The control does not fail because the data is wrong; it fails to stop the site asserting a trend the files cannot carry. It must never be satisfied by narrowing the series until the spread closes.
controls.authority: DATA Act File C (award financial); FPDS-NG contract actions
